HB.Content.Seed.books.apex_patterns.chap: Large quarry spends energy on patrols, displays, feeding, rest, and breeding. Disrupt one expense and the pattern changes elsewhere.
Prey compression, absent scavengers, changed bird height, and abandoned watering points can reveal an apex creature before any direct sign.
HB.Content.Seed.books.apex_patterns.name: Patterns of Apex Predators
HB.Content.Seed.books.apex_patterns.summ: Long-cycle behavior, false retreats, territory inheritance, and human causes of escalation.
HB.Content.Seed.books.bestiary_cartograp: Mark food, water, shelter, barriers, disturbance, and season. A creature's position changes; the reasons for its position form the durable map.
Keep separate layers for confirmed sightings, signs, rumor confidence, weather, human work, and predicted corridors. Contradictions become visible instead of being averaged away.
A field method for mapping ranges that shift with weather, prey, roads, and human disturbance.
HB.Content.Seed.books.field_signs_primer: Record what made the sign, what action produced it, how old it is, and what changed it afterward. Sketch before touching and measure against a fixed object.
A single print proves passage. Repeated feeding, bedding, grooming, and boundary marks establish use of an area. Do not call a trail a lair.
A concise illustrated method for distinguishing passage, feeding, nesting, and territorial signs.
Old Jorek of the North Road
Compare the sign with known leaves, footprints, rain crust, insect activity, and shade. Freshness estimates are local experiments, not universal tables.
Frost can sharpen an old edge, sun can crack a fresh dropping, and wind can refill a track. Record the weather sequence, not only current conditions.
How rain, frost, sun, insects, and wind alter signs over time.
HB.Content.Seed.books.harvest_ledger.cha: Record collector, method, time, preservative, transport, buyer, and final use. Unexplained premium prices often finance poaching or deliberate conflict.
Before taking a rare organ, ask whether shed material, cultivated fungus, livestock tissue, mineral salts, or an alchemical analogue can serve the same function.
HB.Content.Seed.books.harvest_ledger.sum: Yield estimates, spoilage, chain of custody, substitutes, and signs that a buyer is creating the monster problem.
HB.Content.Seed.books.humane_capture.cha: Determine how close the quarry tolerates people, noise, light, barriers, and conspecific scent. A trap inside panic distance begins as a fight.
Account for chest expansion, gills, heat shedding, circulation, horns, wing folds, and the animal's strongest escape direction. Observe continuously and set release criteria.
HB.Content.Seed.books.humane_capture.sum: Planning nonlethal restraint around anatomy, panic distance, breathing, heat, and release routes.
HB.Content.Seed.books.lair_approach.chap: Locate airflow, drainage, refuse, sentry positions, and alternate exits. The safest retreat is decided before the first person enters.
Heat, moisture, prey remains, nesting material, and parasite communities reveal which chamber matters and which can be bypassed.
HB.Content.Seed.books.lair_approach.name: Approaching the Lair
HB.Content.Seed.books.lair_approach.summ: Wind, escape routes, sentries, bait, terrain control, and withdrawal plans.
HB.Content.Seed.books.lair_structures.ch: Cracks, polished contact points, fresh dust, bent roots, water lines, and animal traffic show what carries weight and what recently moved.
A trapped creature tests walls, ceilings, water, and people. Preserve one controlled escape or release route unless containment is the explicit, engineered objective.
HB.Content.Seed.books.lair_structures.su: Reading structural danger before entering burrows, ruins, cliff nests, flooded dens, and root chambers.
HB.Content.Seed.books.monster_anatomy.ch: Photograph or sketch orientation, color, swelling, heat, and surrounding tissue. A valuable gland ruined by contamination is worth less than no sample.
Use distinct tools and containers for venom, heat organs, spores, electrical tissue, and ordinary meat. Label time, location, and collector.
HB.Content.Seed.books.monster_anatomy.su: Safe sampling, trophy preservation, gland handling, and contamination control.
HB.Content.Seed.books.peaceful_hunts.cha: A hunt can end by observation, deterrence, route repair, relocation, negotiated access, capture, or proof that the accused creature is innocent.
Remove the pressure that caused conflict, brief locals, monitor the next cycle, and avoid creating a vacant territory for something worse.
HB.Content.Seed.books.peaceful_hunts.sum: Case studies in deterrence, relocation, habitat repair, and negotiated offerings.
HB.Content.Seed.books.predator_ecology.c: When attacks begin suddenly, inspect prey numbers, water, barriers, breeding grounds, carrion disposal, and new industry before assuming a new predator.
Repairing a route, removing bait, restoring water, or guarding one season may solve what extermination would worsen.
HB.Content.Seed.books.predator_ecology.s: A practical argument for finding ecological causes before declaring extermination.
HB.Content.Seed.books.rumor_craft.author: Inquisitor Emer Vey
HB.Content.Seed.books.rumor_craft.chapte: Ten identical tavern stories may be one story copied nine times. Ask who saw it, who repeated it, and who benefits from the wording.
A false explanation may still preserve accurate time, place, sound, direction, or victim behavior. Separate observation from interpretation.
HB.Content.Seed.books.rumor_craft.name: The Shape of a Useful Rumor
HB.Content.Seed.books.rumor_craft.summar: Separating witnesses, incentives, copied stories, and deliberate cover tales.
HB.Content.Seed.complications.core_compl: The quarry notices the hunters and changes direction.
Rain, wind, or traffic partially destroys the next sign.
A second creature crosses the trail and creates a false lead.
A witness demands payment, protection, or secrecy.
The trail enters private, sacred, or politically sensitive ground.
A sample is hazardous to carry without special containment.
Local hunters have already laid traps that endanger everyone.
The quarry is injured by another cause and behaves unpredictably.
The apparent monster attack hides a human crime.
The lair contains young, eggs, dependents, or symbiotic creatures.
A rival hunting party follows the same lead.
A valuable trophy can be taken only by risking the investigation.
The route crosses a sudden environmental hazard.
An old book contradicts the fresh evidence.
The creature is not the apex threat in this territory.
The next sign is genuine but deliberately placed as a warning.
The trail splits between food, territory, and nesting behavior.
The quarry uses roads, tools, or buildings more intelligently than expected.
A harmless species is being blamed for the real quarry.
Success reveals an urgent time limit.
A well-meaning local destroys the freshest sign while trying to help.
The quarry crosses another creature's territory, mixing both trails.
A buyer offers a suspicious premium for an intact organ.
Sudden weather preserves one clue but erases the route beyond it.
The apparent lair is a seasonal shelter already abandoned.
A rival hunting party uses bait that changes the quarry's behavior.
The trail enters land whose owner forbids access without negotiation.
A dependent juvenile or symbiotic species is discovered near the quarry.
The quarry is following pollution, roadworks, or displaced prey rather than hunting people.
The only safe route passes through a fragile nest, ruin, or water source.

HB.Content.Seed.monsters.ashback_troll.a: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.ashback_troll.b: Normally solitary. It defends heat-rich feeding grounds but can be distracted by salt blocks or fresh charcoal.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.ashback_troll.d: Dense heat-storing plates, long reach, smoke bursts, and rapid recovery while warm.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.ashback_troll.e: It feeds on mineral salts, charcoal, carrion, and resinous wood. It basks before hunting and retreats into cool caves when its back plates overheat.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.ashback_troll.g: A nearby smelter dumps mineral slag into its old feeding ground, driving it toward settlements.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.ashback_troll.h: Heat plates for warming stones; smoke gland for alchemy; ash-black tendon for bowstrings.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.ashback_troll.r: Woodcutters say a walking kiln has begun stealing whole stacks of charcoal.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.ashback_troll.s: charcoal dust mixed with coarse black hair
trees snapped shoulder-high and scorched on one side
A soot-dark giant whose plated back stores heat from fire and sunlight.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.ashback_troll.w: Cooling mud, heavy rain, and attacks beneath the shoulder plates suppress its regeneration.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.bone_orchard_el: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Calm around respectful observers, but the lead bull charges anyone who burns fungi or removes remains from its feeding circuit.
Dense antler crown, disorienting spores, herd feints, and uncanny movement through undergrowth.
The herd carries burial-ground fungi between depleted sites. Its grazing suppresses corpse-bloom outbreaks and returns minerals to living forest.
Grave robbers seeded a nearby ruin with corpse-bloom to conceal their work, disrupting the herd's route.
old battlefields reclaimed by birch forest
ruined grave roads rich in pale fungi
Naturally shed fungal antler shelves for funerary medicines; spore felt; shed hoof keratin.
The dead are being uncovered, but no grave is robbed and white hoofprints circle every open pit.
shallow scrapes exposing old bone without breaking it
white spores caught on branches above head height
A towering elk whose antlers support shelves of bone-white fungi fed by minerals gathered from ancient remains.
Clean running water washes away spores; bells mark herd movement; offerings of mineral salt can redirect a migration.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.carrion_bell_sp: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Retreats from discordant vibration, but attacks creatures that answer its lure tones.
Resonant disorientation, ceiling drops, binding silk, and venom that heightens hearing.
It consumes carrion insects and keeps ossuaries dry. Resonant webs advertise territory and courtship patterns.
Its web records a repeating coded signal from beneath the ruin.
Resonant silk; auditory venom; naturally drilled bone chimes.
The ruined chapel bell rings whenever nobody is looking at it.
clean bones drilled at both ends
web lines that hum in still air
A pale spider that strings hollow bones into resonant webs to lure scavengers.
Packed cloth deadens the web; irregular drumbeats mask movement.
The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Nonpredatory but easily provoked by matching rhythms. A threatened colony answers with a focused pressure wave.
Sonic blast, adhesive tongue, sudden leaps, and concealment beneath floating vegetation.
Its chorus coordinates breeding across distant pools and drives biting insects from nesting sites. The symbiotic frogs clean parasites from its skin.
A nearby bell-founder dumps metal filings into the breeding pool, altering the colony's pitch and causing painful overtones.
marsh shrines and drowned stone circles
Naturally shed resonance membrane for instrument makers; antiseptic skin wax; symbiotic frog eggs under permit.
The swamp has learned a funeral hymn and sings it one verse closer each night.
mud rings vibrating around still footprints
tiny frogs nesting in parallel grooves
broken glass with no impact point
A wagon-sized toad whose ridged back houses resonating air sacs sounded by smaller symbiotic frogs.
Soft cloth baffles disrupt resonance; silence between calls calms the symbionts; cool dry air slows it.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.cinderwing_drak: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Social at roosts, defensive over warm cavities, and attracted to unattended forge heat rather than stored treasure.
Gliding attacks, choking ash fan, ember-coated bite, and excellent grip on vertical stone.
It scavenges fire-killed animals and carries ember mites between geothermal vents. Colonies prevent carrion buildup after eruptions.
The colony moved into trade kilns because its geothermal vent was capped by a roadworks blast.
warm fumarole caves and slag fields
Shed porous scales for heat filters; ember mite cultures; heat-resistant wing membrane scraps.
Every cold kiln in the pass was warm at dawn, though no fuel had been burned.
light bones baked brittle but not charred
warm air pulsing from sealed cracks
A lean gliding drake with porous wing scales that trap embers and release them as defensive ash.
Fine water mist clogs porous scales; sudden cold makes the wings rigid; a prepared warm roost can lure it safely.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.coppercap_jacka: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Bold thieves but reluctant fighters. Packs trade shiny copper for food when they learn a settlement's routines.
Pack feints, irritating spore shake, excellent night coordination, and narrow escape routes.
The fungus extracts trace copper and deters parasites. Packs spread it between ruins and consume rodents poisoned by metal waste.
A fence deliberately feeds the pack to recover valuables from sealed ruins and blames ordinary thieves.
dry ruins where copper coins and pipes corrode
Cultured cap spores for verdigris dyes; shed teeth; parasite-resistant grooming oil.
Green sparks move between the ruins at night, and every missing coin returns bitten in half.
small caches of copper sorted by corrosion
green dust brushed onto shoulder-height stone
paired pawprints circling rather than approaching carrion
A clever jackal carrying copper-green fungal caps along its skull and shoulders, cultivated by pack grooming.
Vinegar scent overwhelms the fungal cues; copper decoys redirect them; isolated animals avoid confrontation.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.dustmantle_burr: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Avoids open air, reacts to rhythmic pounding as a territorial challenge, and surfaces only to shed damaged mantle layers.
Layered earth armor, subterranean charge, dust cloud, and the ability to vanish beneath loose ground.
It follows underground tubers and insect swarms, aerating hard soil but collapsing shallow foundations when migration routes are blocked.
A new stone road cuts the ancient route, concentrating several animals beneath one village.
dry cropland above chalk and clay
wind-carved steppe with abandoned badger warrens
Shed mantle plates for earthen armor; vibration whiskers; digestive grit for stone polish.
A furrow crossed three farms overnight without bending a single fence post.
raised soil ridge with regular breathing vents
chalk dust polished smooth on fence stones
roots clipped from below rather than gnawed
A broad six-limbed burrower wearing a mantle of compacted soil that hardens into layered armor.
Flooded trenches soften its mantle; irregular vibration confuses direction; exposed breathing vents are sensitive.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.embercrop_manti: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Bombards organized groups before diving on isolated targets. It becomes cautious after failed cinder bursts.
Cinder volleys, cliff dives, tail spines, armored chest, and heat haze.
It grinds mineral prey remains in a fermentation crop, spreading heat-loving seeds through cinder waste.
The manticore has begun feeding on slag from a hidden weapons foundry, increasing its explosive range.
Fermentation crop; glass-forming cinder; heatproof mane fibers.
Stonecutters find arrows fused into glass before hearing wings overhead.
regurgitated black gravel smelling of vinegar
A leonine cliff predator whose throat crop ferments mineral grit into explosive cinders.
Alkaline dust disrupts crop fermentation; baited heavy nets exploit its committed dive.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.fen_lantern_mot: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Curious toward warm lamps. Swarms redirect intruders away from nesting pools but may accidentally lead them into deep water.
Dazzling pulses, choking scale clouds, and false-lantern formations.
Larvae consume rot and corpse wax. Adults pollinate night reeds and use coordinated light to deter predators.
The swarm is clustering around an illegally buried alchemical corpse.
Luminous scale powder; wax-eating larvae for mortuary work; intact light sacs.
A line of lanterns leads night travelers safely across the fen—until the last light turns around.
spiral flight marks in low fog
small frogs gathered beneath dead lamps
A hand-sized moth whose abdomen carries blue marsh-light and whose swarms imitate distant lanterns.
Covered red light attracts without triggering defensive pulses; rain weighs down their scales.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.gloamfang_couga: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Avoids broad even illumination. It stalks from alternating cover and may abandon a hunt when prey controls the light.
Shadow-to-shadow leaps, silence, throat strikes, and false eye-shine.
It hunts along moving shade and limits cliff-goat populations. Kittens learn routes by following sunset bands.
A logging operation removed the cougar’s normal migration corridor and trapped it near livestock.
ravines where sunlight reaches only briefly
Light-sensitive whiskers; matte hide; dusk-adapted eye fluid.
Goats disappear only when their shadows touch the treeline.
prey dragged along the boundary of light
A black mountain cat whose whiskers sense the edges of light and shadow.
Diffuse lantern screens erase sharp shadow edges; mirrored ground reveals landing positions.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.gravewind_hyena: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Tests confidence through circling calls. It attacks those who break formation or imitate the alpha whistle incorrectly.
Pack flanking, disorienting whistles, bone-spitting shakes, and relentless pursuit.
Packs consume carrion exposed by shifting sand and disperse disease-resistant gut flora. They follow seasonal war winds carrying scent.
A battlefield excavator deliberately exposes graves to drive travelers away from a smuggling route.
dry battlefields and exposed tomb roads
Whistling mane tubes; disease-resistant bile; lightweight bone needles.
At sunset, the dead laugh from the old road and answer anyone who laughs back.
bone splinters woven into coarse mane hair
carcasses opened only on the leeward side
A long-legged pack scavenger whose hollow mane whistles through bone fragments.
Crosswinds ruin their whistle coordination; burying or burning exposed bone caches forces relocation.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.hollow_eyed_wyr: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Investigates rhythm and air pressure before attacking. It may ignore motionless creatures inside turbulent airflow.
Stone-swimming bursts, constriction, pressure roars, and nearly impenetrable dorsal scales.
It regulates deep cave populations and follows seasonal pressure shifts. Its tunnels can reconnect sealed aquifers.
It is fleeing an even larger subterranean migration rather than expanding its territory.
mine networks with strong air currents
Pressure membranes; resonant teeth; dense scale plates.
Miners hear their own footsteps returning from tunnels that have not been dug.
echoes arriving before the original sound
prey bones packed into air shafts
A blind serpentine apex predator that maps caverns through pressure-sensitive eye hollows.
Conflicting air currents overload its sensory hollows; soft packed clay prevents stone-swimming.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.ironjaw_lindwor: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Collects resonant metal and guards underwater caches. It bargains through offerings more readily than most drakes.
Iron bite, tail sweeps, underwater charges, and magnetic jaw snaps that pull loose weapons.
It ingests iron to reinforce jaw plates used for cracking river boulders and exposing mineral algae.
The lindworm is repairing a flood barrier built by its ancestors; removing it risks the valley.
Magnetic jaw filings; armored throat hide; mineral-digesting gut stones.
A bridge toll collector accepts only bent nails and never shows his face.
drag furrows ending at deep water
A two-limbed river drake with iron-coated jaw plates and a taste for worked metal.
Nonmetallic weapons avoid magnetic control; sour tannin washes weaken fresh iron plating.
The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Curious toward light, violent when trapped, and otherwise more scavenger than hunter of people.
Slippery body, electrical pulse at close range, tight turning radius, and darkness.
It follows seasonal cave floods and keeps fish populations moving between isolated pools. Large specimens sometimes enter surface waters after heavy rain.
Illegal dye waste has blinded the surface fish, drawing the eels toward the millpond in unusual numbers.
deep millponds connected to cave systems
Lure sac for cold lamps; insulating skin oil; jaw cartilage for flexible instruments.
Blue lamps drift beneath the millpond, and every lamp faces the same way when someone drowns.
crescent bite marks on submerged timber
blue mucus glowing for several minutes
shoals of fish pressed into unnatural corners
A long pale eel whose hinged lower jaw carries a blue lure used to herd blind cave fish.
Steady warm light overrides its lure; woven nets catch the jaw fins; shallow flowing water prevents effective turning.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.mireglass_basil: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Patient ambusher. It circles reflective water before striking and withdraws when deprived of mirrored surfaces.
Distorting reflections, paralytic venom, armored brow, and sudden lateral charges.
It filters mineral-rich water through throat sacs and hunts warm-blooded prey at dawn. Shed scales slowly dissolve, enriching the bog.
Its apparent petrification is a reversible mineral paralysis if treated within one day.
sunken roads bordered by pale reeds
Reflective scales for lenses; venom for antitoxin research; throat crystal for divination tools.
Travelers vanish beside puddles that reflect a sky different from the one overhead.
small animals stiffened but not decayed
A low, many-legged marsh predator whose translucent scales reflect hostile movement.
Ash, chalk, or disturbed mud clouds its reflective scales; throat sacs are vulnerable while it drinks.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.mirrorhide_lynx: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Avoids groups that maintain eye contact and spacing, but stalks isolated movement. It retrieves reflective objects taken from its den.
Optical camouflage, false reflected positions, pouncing force, and near-silent footing.
It hunts overabundant cliff goats and collects reflective stones to line dens. Older cats regulate territory through visual displays rather than combat.
The lynx is recovering plates stolen by an antiquarian who believes they are pieces of a lost mirror.
misty conifer slopes above still tarns
Only naturally shed mirror plates should be taken; whiskers for optical instruments; den quartz after relocation.
A hunter fired at his own reflection between the pines, and something else carried the arrow away.
tracks visible only when viewed from the side
prey staring at empty mirrored water
A silent great cat with thin reflective plates beneath its fur that borrow colors and movement from the surroundings.
Matte charcoal dust outlines the plates; diffuse lantern light reduces reflections; rhythmic group movement denies isolated targets.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.moonveil_stag.a: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.moonveil_stag.b: Avoids violence unless cornered or its route is blocked. It tests pursuers with loops and time-lost clearings.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.moonveil_stag.d: Path distortion, blinding mist, antler sweeps, and short spatial leaps.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.moonveil_stag.e: It grazes on night-blooming plants and spreads their seeds through cold mist. Its routes stabilize thin places between worlds.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.moonveil_stag.g: It is maintaining a failing boundary seal. Killing it opens a dangerous crossing within three nights.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.moonveil_stag.h: Shed antler dust for navigation charms; moonmoss from bedding sites; never requires killing.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.moonveil_stag.r: A wounded hunter followed silver hoofprints and returned before he had left.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.moonveil_stag.s: moss growing toward an empty trail
A pale stag whose antlers trail cold luminous mist and bend nearby paths.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.moonveil_stag.w: Continuous bells, chalked route markers, and sunlight reflected from polished copper anchor local paths.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.reed_crowned_cr: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Patient and strongly nest-bound. It prefers warning tail slaps when eggs are not threatened but attacks boats that cut through its reed nursery.
Submerged approach, crushing bite, armored back, and sudden lateral tail strikes.
The crown shelters insects, frogs, and hatchlings. Adults prune waterways and create open pools used by many wetland species.
The animal's old basking bank was walled off by a new mill, forcing it into the ferry channel.
slow rivers choked with reed islands
flooded rice fields and abandoned canals
Regrown crown reeds for water filters; shed scutes for shields; nonlethal collection of antiseptic nest moss.
A whole patch of reeds moved upstream against the current and took a ferryman with it.
reed roots cut cleanly below the waterline
broad belly furrows ending in still water
fish scales caught high in floating vegetation
An immense crocodilian that cultivates living reed mats across its armored back as camouflage and nursery.
Dry ground exposes its weight; bitter smoke drives symbiotic insects from the crown and distracts it; eggs can be moved safely with expert handling.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.rimehorn_auroch: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Forms a defensive ring around calves. Solitary bulls challenge large moving shapes but tolerate slow low profiles.
Ice-horn sweeps, trampling formation, freezing breath, and thick insulating hide.
Herds open winter grazing paths used by smaller animals. Ice horns condense scarce water during dry cold seasons.
A magical weather vane forces the herd into the pass by redirecting prevailing winds.
Insulating wool; meltwater horn cores; cold-resistant fat.
A caravan road freezes from hoofprint to hoofprint even under clear summer skies.
grass cut cleanly beneath frozen arcs
broad hoofprints rimmed with white crystals
windbreak hollows packed with shed wool
A shaggy wild ox whose horn cores freeze moisture into layered ice blades.
Dry heat cracks horn ice; separated leaders can be redirected with mineral salt.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.saltmarsh_mirec: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Retreats from steady vibration but attacks isolated movement. Colonies exchange warning knocks through mud.
Burrowing ambushes, crushing claws, mud jets, and overlapping shell plates.
It cleans tidal flats of carrion and shellfish. Breeding colonies can undermine roads during spring tides.
The current attacks are caused by stolen nesting stones used in a new harbor wall.
tidal mudflats and salt reed beds
Saltproof shell; vibration bladders; sweet claw meat.
Salt workers claim the mud has learned to cut ropes and open barrels.
paired crescent cuts in rope and reeds
A broad armored scavenger that tunnels beneath wet ground and hears through brine-filled leg chambers.
Dry sand clogs leg chambers; rhythmic stamping can herd it toward prepared ground.
The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
It tests intruders with warning dives before committing. During calm weather it is cautious; during storms it becomes bold and nearly tireless.
Extreme altitude, electrified plumage, concussive wingbeats, and excellent vision through rain.
It hunts cliff ungulates and large fish, then grinds conductive minerals into its nesting shelf. Stored charge helps incubate its eggs through cold squalls.
A lighthouse lens recently installed below the nest flashes like a rival roc's courtship display and provokes the attacks.
high ridges struck repeatedly by lightning
Stormglass vanes for capacitors and weather charms; hollow wing bones for resonant horns; conductive talon sheath.
Sailors claim the thunder now circles one particular cliff before every wreck.
glasslike feather splinters magnetized to iron
spiral scorch marks on exposed rock
goat carcasses lifted without drag marks
A vast cliff-nesting bird whose translucent pinions store static charge and sing before storms.
Grounded metal lines drain its charge; wet clay fouls the glass feathers; protecting the nest can be used to redirect rather than kill it.
The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Protective of piglets and feeding sites. A warning consists of three ground scrapes before a charge.
Thorn armor, crushing charge, and coordinated herd feints.
Family groups migrate between ironroot patches. Their rooting aerates hard soil but can destroy crops within hours.
The dominant sow, not the largest boar, controls the herd route.
Flexible thorn hide; ironroot tusks; rich fat used in weatherproofing.
Farmers find fences woven shut overnight with bloody brambles.
bark polished and pierced by side rubbing
root pits lined with red saliva
A massive boar whose hide grows living thorn mats after feeding on ironroot.
Wet leather blankets snag and flatten the thorns; loud metallic ringing breaks herd coordination.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.veinroot_coloss: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Slow, purposeful, and uninterested in prey. It dismantles the source of harm and uses debris to dam contaminated water.
Massive rooted body, mineral plates, grasping root cables, and rapid repair while touching living soil.
It redistributes trace minerals through fungal and root networks, awakening only after severe extraction, fire, or poisoned runoff.
The colossus is responding to arsenic runoff, not ordinary mining; a rival company sabotaged the drainage channel.
landslide scars where bedrock lies exposed
Only fallen ore bark should be collected: living root fiber, catalytic nodules, and restorative sap.
The mine supports were found neatly woven into a tree line half a mile uphill.
metal dust arranged in rootlike veins
trees leaning toward a moving underground pressure
square-cut timbers returned with living bark
A walking root mass armored with ore nodules and animated when its forest's mineral network is threatened.
Salted stone interrupts root contact; restoring clean water can pacify it; exposed fungal heart-knots direct its motion.
HB.Content.Seed.monsters.whitewake_serpe: The built-in catalogue is system-neutral and intentionally contains no unverified combat statistics.
Migratory, rarely aggressive away from calves, but follows vessels whose hull vibrations resemble its herd calls.
Great mass, submerged speed, freezing spray, and the ability to coil around ships without surfacing.
It follows spawning fish and keeps open lanes through young ice. Its shed scales create mineral nurseries for shellfish.
A new harbor foghorn reproduces a calf distress frequency and keeps drawing the same adult into shipping lanes.
pack-ice channels and deep coastal shelves
Shed keel scales for cold-resistant plating; mineral foam salts; naturally lost whisker filaments for navigation tools.
A wake crossed the bay for an hour, but no mast, fin, or breath ever broke the surface.
foam holding a faint mineral taste
fish schools divided into two clean lanes
ice scored from below in paired arcs
A pale sea serpent whose keeled scales aerate the water into a long white trail visible from shore.
Low irregular drumbeats break mistaken following behavior; warm shallow water exhausts it; sensitive lateral keels reveal its turns.

HB.GM.Title: Hunt Administration
HB.Guide.GM.Approvals1: Rumor gathering and track searches: approve one attempt only when the character has time, access, a location, witnesses, signs, or another believable opportunity.
HB.Guide.GM.Approvals2: Hunt steps: approve one attempt when the party has reached the situation represented by the active step. A failed attempt does not automatically authorize a reroll.
HB.Guide.GM.Approvals3: Sightings and trophies: players may record them at any time, but automatic knowledge credit is queued separately. Approve credit only when the evidence is meaningful and not a duplicate.
HB.Guide.GM.Approvals4: Share Insight: players may share freely, but a sender can award the same target only once per quarry knowledge stage. This preserves cooperation without turning repeated clicks into points.
HB.Guide.GM.ApprovalsText: The default approval setting protects campaign pacing without making the GM click every harmless journal action. It gates actions that can reveal new information or advance a shared hunt.
HB.Guide.GM.GMOwnText: Create and edit quarry; expose or withhold reference material; create, assign, pause, edit, advance, or resolve hunts; configure roll and permission settings; install generated library content; provision Actors; change shared monster images; adjust knowledge directly; approve repeatable player fieldwork; adjudicate secret truth and complications; and manage provider content.
HB.Guide.GM.Intro: The GM owns hidden truth and progression authority; players own most routine record-keeping and can execute approved actions themselves. The module is designed so useful player curiosity cannot become unlimited mechanical progress.
HB.Guide.GM.PlayerOwnText: Open their Bestiary; choose their hunter; read unlocked knowledge; add and remove personal notes; record sightings; record trophies or samples; read available books; publish their personal journal; inspect assigned hunts; choose a permitted skill; execute a GM-approved fieldwork or hunt attempt; and share an insight. Repeated sharing at the same knowledge stage cannot award the same target again.
HB.Guide.GM.PlayerOwnTitle: Players can handle on their own
HB.Guide.GM.RolesText: Treat the dashboard as a division of responsibilities, not as a replacement for table conversation. Players can inspect what they have learned and maintain their own field journal. The GM decides when the fiction provides a new information-gathering opportunity, what secret information is true, and when a hunt can advance.
HB.Guide.GM.SessionText: Ask players to describe what they are doing before they request a mechanical opportunity. Approve the action after the fictional approach is established, then let the player perform the roll from their dashboard. After the result, narrate what changes. The dashboard should record and support the scene, not replace roleplay or adjudication.
HB.Guide.GM.Title: Complete GM guide
HB.Guide.GM.Workflow1: Seed the fiction first: introduce a patron, disappearance, carcass, witness, rumor, book, territory change, or other reason for the party to care.
HB.Guide.GM.Workflow2: Create and assign the hunt when the party meaningfully commits. Pick the quarry and trail template, set stakes and region, and assign only the participating Foundry users.
HB.Guide.GM.Workflow3: Let players drive routine investigation. They can request rumors, tracks, or the next hunt-step attempt when they have a fictional reason. Approve one opportunity when the scene, time, access, and approach justify it.
HB.Guide.GM.Workflow4: Resolve consequences in the fiction. A failed roll should cost time, expose danger, create a complication, consume access, or change the situation rather than simply invite immediate identical rerolls.
HB.Guide.GM.Workflow5: Use sightings, trophies, books, observations, and successful hunt stages to award knowledge when they represent genuinely new information. Player evidence is recordable immediately, while automatic credit is separated behind GM review.
HB.Guide.GM.Workflow6: Conclude deliberately. Resolve the hunt when the party has actually achieved or lost the objective, record the outcome, then allow the resulting knowledge, trophies, reputation, or follow-up hooks to matter later.
HB.Guide.GM.Workflow7: At the conclusion, let the player choose the desired outcome. Apply the configured automatic, check-plus-GM, or GM-only resolution policy and record the actual scene outcome rather than a preselected result.
HB.Guide.GM.WorkflowTitle: A hunt from setup to aftermath
HB.Guide.Intro: The module turns finding a creature into a playable investigation rather than a single Survival roll.
HB.Guide.PermissionsText: The GM controls monster definitions, secret truth, shared hunts, and generated reference documents. Each player controls their own notes and personal Bestiary progress. Players cannot inspect another player's private record.
HB.Guide.Player.ApprovalsText: Rumors, track searches, and hunt stages depend on the current fictional situation. A request tells the GM that you are ready to try. Approval is not a reward and does not guarantee success; it means the opportunity exists now. It is consumed by one attempt, which prevents accidental progress from repeated clicking.
HB.Guide.Player.Intro: You can manage almost all of your own field journal and perform approved investigation actions without seeing GM-only information. The module intentionally separates recording what your character does from deciding when a new discovery or hunt step is available.
HB.Guide.Player.SelfServiceText: You can browse everything your character has unlocked, maintain private notes, record observations and specimens, inspect assigned hunts, read sources the campaign makes available, publish your personal journal, export your own progress, and prepare a fieldwork request. These actions do not reveal hidden GM truth simply because you click around.
HB.Guide.Player.SelfServiceTitle: What you can do without asking for a button permission
HB.Guide.Player.TableTalkText: Say where you search, whom you question, what evidence you use, what risk you accept, or how you approach the active hunt stage. The GM decides whether that creates an opportunity and may ask for a different approach. Use the dashboard after that conversation to execute and record the action.
HB.Guide.Player.TableTalkTitle: What to discuss with the GM
HB.Guide.Player.Title: Detailed player guide
HB.Guide.Player.Workflow1: Choose your hunter by controlling exactly one token or by using the Actor assigned to your Foundry user.
HB.Guide.Player.Workflow2: Use your Bestiary, available books, party discussion, and assigned hunt to decide what your character wants to investigate next.
HB.Guide.Player.Workflow3: When you want to gather a new rumor, search for tracks, or attempt the active hunt step, describe the approach at the table and request the opportunity in the dashboard. One approval unlocks one attempt.
HB.Guide.Player.Workflow4: Make the approved roll yourself. Success or failure is recorded through the normal module workflow; an identical reroll is not automatically available unless the GM approves another opportunity.
HB.Guide.Player.Workflow5: Record what happened: add notes, sightings, trophies or samples, read acquired books, share useful knowledge, and publish your personal Bestiary journal whenever useful.
HB.Guide.Player.Workflow6: At the final hunt stage, choose what you are trying to accomplish. Some outcomes resolve directly, some require a check, and others require the GM to confirm what actually happened in the scene.
HB.Guide.Step1Text: A rumor, book, witness, or old trophy introduces a possible beast without revealing the whole entry.
HB.Guide.Step2Text: Tracks, feeding sites, residue, calls, nests, and false leads reveal habitat and behavior.
HB.Guide.Step3Text: Each hunt is a short questline of checks, decisions, hazards, complications, and changing information.
HB.Guide.Step4Text: Slay, capture, drive away, relocate, observe, or negotiate—then record sightings, trophies, and lessons.
